questions.question: Which are Scaleway Regions? Choose three.
questions.explanation: The Scaleway documentation lists Paris (fr-par), Amsterdam (nl-ams) and Warsaw (pl-waw) among its Regions.

questions.question: Which Scaleway support plan includes a Technical Account Manager?
questions.explanation: Only the Enterprise plan includes a Technical Account Manager, together with quarterly technical reviews and an architecture audit.

questions.question: Which tool describes Scaleway resources in configuration files and deploys declaratively as IaC?
options: Terraform or OpenTofu with Scaleway provider
questions.explanation: Terraform and OpenTofu are Infrastructure as Code tools used to deploy Scaleway resources declaratively, whereas the CLI is a command-line tool built on the Scaleway API.

questions.question: True or false: using less than committed in a savings plan means billing only actual consumption.
questions.explanation: With a savings plan you are still billed the committed amount (with the discount applied) when you use less, and usage above it is charged at standard prices.

questions.question: What is an IAM application?
options: A non-human user in an Organization that can hold API keys not linked to a person
A group of users sharing the same policy
A preinstalled software image for Instances
A permission set restricted to a single Project
questions.explanation: An IAM application is a non-human user used to create API keys that are not linked to a human user; it has no access to the Scaleway console.

questions.question: Which two elements make up an IAM policy rule?
questions.explanation: Each IAM rule consists of a scope and one or more permission sets, plus optional conditions.

questions.question: Which scope must a policy rule use to grant access to billing and IAM features?
questions.explanation: Billing, IAM, Project management and support are managed at Organization level, so the Organization scope is required to give access to them.

questions.question: True or false: a single Project can group resources in different Regions.
questions.explanation: Projects are cross-regional: resources located in different Regions can be grouped in one Project.

questions.question: Who implements backup strategy, including cross-Region replication, for Object Storage data?
options: A third-party partner appointed by Scaleway
questions.explanation: Under the storage shared responsibility model, internal resiliency does not protect against accidental deletion, so the customer must set up external backups and cross-region replication.

questions.question: Which two situations require spreading resources across several Regions rather than only AZs?
options: Tolerating a power outage in a single data center
Protecting against a regional outage such as a natural disaster
Low-latency replication with fast failover between nearby sites
Keeping backups in a physically separate location
questions.explanation: Multi-region is recommended for regional outages and for backup and recovery in a physically separate location, while multi-AZ covers localized failures and low-latency failover.

questions.question: What best describes an Elastic Metal server?
options: A virtual machine with shared resources
A dedicated physical server for a single tenant
questions.explanation: Elastic Metal servers are on-demand, 100% dedicated physical machines without a hypervisor.

questions.question: Which Elastic Metal range has large local storage for data protection?
questions.explanation: Lithium servers are designed with huge Local Storage, while Beryllium targets production-grade applications and Iridium high-workload applications.

questions.question: What is Scaleway Apple silicon as-a-Service built on, and what is it for?
options: Mac mini hardware for developing, building, testing and signing apps for Apple devices
Mac Pro towers for video rendering
iPhone device farms for hosting mobile games
Mac mini hardware for hosting Windows virtual desktops
questions.explanation: Apple silicon as-a-Service uses Apple Mac mini hardware and is tailored for developing, building, testing and signing applications for Apple devices.

questions.question: Which two statements about InterLink are correct?
options: Secure private link between external infrastructure and VPC, off public internet
One InterLink per VPC, same Region
questions.explanation: InterLink is a private connection between external infrastructure and a VPC that bypasses the public internet, and each InterLink attaches to one VPC in the same region.

questions.question: To back up only an Instance data volume, not the whole Instance, which resource should you create?
questions.explanation: A snapshot captures a single volume at one point in time, whereas an image is a complete backup of the Instance with all its volumes.

questions.question: Which volume types can a Scaleway Instance use for storage?
options: Object Storage buckets and Glacier archives
Container Registry namespaces and Dedibackup spaces
questions.explanation: Instances use local volumes (SSD storage on the hypervisor, with a size fixed by the Instance type) or network-attached block volumes, and some types boot directly on block volumes.

questions.question: What distinguishes a GPU Instance from other Scaleway Instances?
options: It includes GPU hardware for AI/ML workloads
It is billed per minute only
questions.explanation: GPU Instances are Instances equipped with dedicated high-end NVIDIA graphics processing units.

questions.question: An Instance is powered off (not standby). Which three statements apply?
options: Flexible IP continues to be billed
Block Storage continues to be billed
questions.explanation: When a server is powered off, only its volumes and any reserved flexible IP address are billed.

questions.question: Which workload fits Instances with dedicated vCPUs rather than shared vCPUs?
questions.explanation: Dedicated vCPUs give consistent and predictable performance for production and latency-sensitive workloads, while shared vCPUs suit development, staging and non-critical workloads at a lower cost.

questions.question: Which statement about SSH keys for Instance access is correct?
options: SSH keys are stored in the Instance metadata
SSH keys can be managed via IAM
SSH keys are only for Linux Instances
questions.explanation: The public key is kept in your Scaleway account and passed to the Instance at boot, while the private key stays securely on the computer you connect from.

questions.question: Which Instance feature allows restarting the server over the network using a minimal OS for debugging and system data recovery?
questions.explanation: Rescue mode restarts your server via the network on a minimal OS to debug it and recover system data; the server must be running to switch to it.

questions.question: Which Serverless product runs batch workloads over longer durations?
questions.explanation: Serverless Jobs is designed for batch jobs and tasks that need to run to completion, such as data processing or migrations.

questions.question: A Serverless Function has min-scale 0. What happens after idle periods?
options: It keeps running at minimum cost
It switches to a paid tier
questions.explanation: With a minimum scale of 0, Functions scale down to zero active instances while idle and do not consume resources, which reduces cost.

questions.question: Which three can trigger a Serverless Function? Choose three.
questions.explanation: Functions can be triggered by HTTP requests, CRON schedules and messages from a queue (or a NATS subject).

questions.question: Where should a stateless Serverless Function store data that must be kept?
questions.explanation: Serverless Functions are stateless and keep no state between executions, so persistent data goes to services such as Object Storage, Managed Databases or Serverless SQL Databases.

questions.question: Which service provides network-attached volumes that behave like regular disks?
questions.explanation: Block volumes are network-attached storage that you can plug in and out of Instances like a virtual hard drive.

questions.question: How is a Block Storage volume billed?
questions.explanation: Block Storage is billed by the hour based on the size of the volume, not on the data actually stored on it.

questions.question: Which two statements about Object Storage bucket versioning are correct?
options: Versioning keeps multiple versions of an object
Versioning can be suspended but not reversed
Each version has its own key
Versioning doubles storage costs for each version
questions.explanation: Non-current versions remain stored and billable and can be retrieved by version ID, and a bucket whose versioning was enabled can only move to Suspended, not back to Unversioned.

questions.question: Which Object Storage class is best for secondary backup copies?
questions.explanation: Glacier is the Object Storage class best suited for secondary backup copies and long-term retention, as it provides the most cost-effective storage for data that is accessed infrequently.

questions.question: Which Object Storage feature applies write-once-read-many (WORM) mode?
questions.explanation: Object lock uses a WORM model to prevent deletion or overwriting for a fixed period or indefinitely, and it requires versioning to be enabled on the bucket.

questions.question: Resources on the same Private Network can be located in which scope?
questions.explanation: Private Networks connect resources across multiple Availability Zones within the same region, and all Private Networks are now regional.

questions.question: Which two features does a Public Gateway provide?
questions.explanation: Public Gateways sit at the border of Private Networks and offer NAT as well as an SSH bastion.

questions.question: How does a Load Balancer maintain application availability when a backend server fails?
options: Reinstalls the OS on the failed server
Replicates server data to another Region
Uses health checks to stop sending requests to unhealthy servers
Forces clients to reconnect through a Public Gateway
questions.explanation: The Load Balancer monitors backend servers with health checks and, when a server is down, rebalances the load between the remaining servers.

questions.question: Do Load Balancer backend servers need public IP addresses?
questions.explanation: The Load Balancer can address backend servers by their private IP addresses over a Private Network (required for a private Load Balancer) and can reach any backend server in the same VPC this way, so a public IP is not required.

questions.question: To which resource can a flexible IP created for Instances be moved?
questions.explanation: Flexible IPs are tied to a product category: an Instance flexible IP can be moved to another Instance but not to a Load Balancer, a Public Gateway or an Elastic Metal server.

questions.question: How is a flexible IP billed when reserved but not attached?
options: Billed as long as reservation is open
questions.explanation: A flexible IP is billed from the moment you reserve it until you cancel the reservation, whether you are effectively using it or not.

questions.question: Can you run queries on the standby node of HA Managed Database for PostgreSQL?
questions.explanation: The standby node is a hot standby that takes over only if the main node fails; read-only queries require a Read Replica.

questions.question: Which Managed Database feature gives a read-only live copy to offload read traffic?
questions.explanation: A Read Replica is a live copy of a Database Instance that only allows read-only connections, whereas a snapshot or a clone is a point-in-time copy.

questions.question: Which statement about Serverless SQL Database billing is correct?
options: Storage is free while database is idle
Compute is billed at full rate even when idle
Storage always billed, idle DB with 0 minimum vCPU has no compute cost
questions.explanation: Storage is billed whether the database is active or idle, and you are not billed for compute if the database has 0 vCPU as a minimum and is idle.

questions.question: True or false: once encryption at rest is activated on Managed Database, it cannot be disabled.
questions.explanation: The documentation states that, once activated on a Database Instance, encryption at rest cannot be disabled.

questions.question: Which Scaleway managed Kubernetes service connects nodes from other cloud providers?
questions.explanation: Kosmos is the multi-cloud Kubernetes service, while Kapsule clusters are composed only of Scaleway Instances.

questions.question: Which Scaleway product provides automated monitoring of a Kapsule cluster?
questions.explanation: Cockpit provides automated monitoring of a Kapsule cluster, with metrics visualized in a hosted Grafana.

questions.question: Which two statements about Container Registry are correct?
options: A namespace is a collection of container images
Images are always public and cannot be restricted
An image can be public, private or inherit namespace privacy
Container Registry stores Kubernetes cluster state
questions.explanation: A namespace is a collection of container images, and an image can be public, private or inherit the privacy policy of its namespace.

questions.question: Which three data types can Cockpit collect and store? Choose three.
questions.explanation: Cockpit stores three data types: metrics, logs and traces.

questions.question: How many Cockpits can a Scaleway Project have?
questions.explanation: Cockpits are scoped per Project, and a Scaleway Project can have only one Cockpit.

questions.question: Which product records actions performed by principals on Organization resources?
questions.explanation: Audit Trail holds a record of events and changes performed within a Scaleway Organization, whether the actions were successful, attempted or failed.

questions.question: Under which name is the former Scaleway Managed Inference product now offered?
questions.explanation: Managed Inference was renamed Generative APIs - Dedicated Deployment; it is the same product under a new name.

questions.question: In Scaleway Queues, what receives messages that cannot be delivered to their destination queue?
questions.explanation: A dead-letter queue receives and holds undelivered messages, and it must be of the same type, in the same Project and region as the queues it serves.

questions.question: Which Scaleway Queues queue type should be used when exact message order matters and duplicates are not tolerated?
questions.explanation: FIFO queues preserve the exact order of messages and do not tolerate duplicates, which suits cases such as order management.
